messages.author: d54aba6af40f8c5e
messages.subject: zero-inflated gaussian
parts:
Hello,

I have some, generally, positive outcome data with a lot of "true" zeros. I was thinking of modeling them with some sort of zero-inflated gaussian model. Is such a model available with INLA?

Thanks in advance,

John

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] zero-inflated gaussian
parts:
yes, do

inla.doc("poission")

and it will pop up.

if the non-zero part is like f(y|y>0) , then you have also use a two
likelihood approach and have a proper model for the zero part and the
non-zero part (see the example in the SPDE book online)
